definition: A separate, typically smaller model used specifically to check the inputs or outputs of a primary model against safety or policy constraints.
details: Guardrail models offload safety-related classification from the main generative model, allowing dedicated, often faster and more specialized filtering as part of a layered safety architecture.
story: Picture guardrails on a mountain road — not there to slow you down on the straightaways, but to keep you from flying off the cliff. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Think of it as the quiet rule that a tool should be useful without being dangerous. It is the difference between “it works” and “it is safe to put in front of people.” That deliberate caution is Guardrail Model.
